# 1 Clement Chapter 18 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 18 is the Miserere (Psalm 51/LXX 50) — the great penitential psalm of David. Clement cites it as the supreme expression of humble confession. The chapter occupies a pivotal position in the argument: if David, attested as "a man after God's own heart," confessed his unworthiness so profoundly, how much more should the Corinthians humble themselves?

The LXX text cited by Clement is very close to the standard LXX Psalm 50 but with some variations. Key divergences from the standard LXX noted in the disagreements below.

The famous v.17 ("The sacrifice of God is a broken spirit") becomes Clement's summary: the Corinthians must offer God the sacrifice of a broken, humble heart rather than continuing in their proud contention.

---

## Chapter 18

**18:1** But what shall we say of David, who received attestation, and of whom God said: "I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, whom I have anointed with eternal mercy"? [Ps 89:20; 1 Sam 13:14]

**18:2** But even he says to God: "Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy; and according to the abundance of your compassion blot out my transgression.

**18:3** Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is before me continually.

**18:4** Against you only have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight; so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.

**18:5** For behold, I was conceived in iniquity, and in sin my mother bore me.

**18:6** For behold, you have loved truth; the hidden and secret things of your wisdom you have made manifest to me.

**18:7** You shall purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean; you shall wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

**18:8** You shall make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

**18:9** Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

**18:10** Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

**18:11** Cast me not away from your presence, and take not your holy spirit from me.

**18:12** Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.

**18:13** I will teach transgressors your ways, and the ungodly shall turn to you.

**18:14** Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation; my tongue shall sing of your righteousness.

**18:15** Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praise.

**18:16** For if you had desired sacrifice, I would have given it; with burnt offerings you will not be pleased.

**18:17** A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise." [Ps 51:1-17 LXX]

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
